cases.purpose: pr -t with stdin and stdout on one private terminal held open: each completed line is written before the next is typed, and nothing is left for EOF; bytes match GNU pr.
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils pr 9.7 (reference PATH) on the same feeder.
cases.comparison: byte parity vs GNU pr of each delivery phase; exact expectations for -t

cases.purpose: pr -l 12 -h HDR -D X (fixed header text and date string) on a private terminal held open: the 12-line first page (header, two body lines, trailer) is complete once the second line is typed, before the third line and EOF; every delivery phase matches GNU pr byte for byte.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 feed.py "$BASH" 'pr -l 12 -h HDR -D X' pty pty 610a 620a 630a > status
IFS= read -r -d '' page < cum2
n=${page//[!$'\n']/}
(( ${#n} >= 12 )) && echo page1-before-eof > mark || echo "page1-lines ${#n}" > mark
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils pr 9.7 (reference PATH) on the same feeder.
cases.comparison: byte parity vs GNU pr of each delivery phase; semantic marker: at least 12 newline-terminated lines delivered after the second body line

cases.purpose: pr -t -a -2 -w 20 on a private terminal held open: the first across row ('aa' and 'bb') is delivered with its newline after the second line is typed and before the third; all phases match GNU pr.
cases.script:
/usr/bin/python3 feed.py "$BASH" 'pr -t -a -2 -w 20' pty pty 61610a 62620a 63630a > status
IFS= read -r -d '' row < cum2
[[ $row == *aa*bb*$'\n' && $row != *cc* ]] && echo row1-before-eof > mark || echo row1-missing > mark
cases.oracle: GNU coreutils pr 9.7 (reference PATH) on the same feeder.
cases.comparison: byte parity vs GNU pr of each delivery phase; semantic marker for the completed row before EOF
